programme.title: How Do They Do It S13 - "Pulverizer/Bomber Jackets/Lambic Beer/"
programme.desc: How do they forge a set of jaws that can chomp through concrete and demolish tower blocks? How do they stitch the historic airman’s bomber? How do they brew the oldest beer in the Western World?

programme.title: How Do They Do It S13 - "Sydney Opera House/Handsaws/Microphones/Icebreaker"
programme.desc: How do they cool Sydney’s famous Opera House? How do they turn Sheffield steel into a carpenter’s handsaw? How do they make a microphone that can pick up a whisper? How do they steer a safe course through a frozen river?

programme.title: How Do They Do It S13 - "Moonshine/e-bikes/Wetsuits"
programme.desc: How do they brew moonshine in the heart of New York City? How do they make a battery powered bicycle that can do nearly 30mph? How do they grow the rubber for wetsuits in the Arizona desert?

programme.title: How Do They Do It S13 - "Gemstones/Cowboy Boots/Road Sweepers"
programme.desc: How do they mine one of the rarest gemstones in the world? How do they craft the classic cowboy boot? How do they build a monster road sweeper that can pick up 7 tonnes of trash?

programme.title: How Do They Do It S13 - "Duvets/Drill Pipes/Rubber Bands"
programme.desc: How do they make the world’s softest duvets? How do they drill for oil thousands of metres below ground? How do they put the stretch in the world’s stretchiest rubber bands?

programme.title: Bright Now S1 - "Path to the Pros"
programme.desc: What does it take to become a professional tennis player? Both on and off the court preparations help build the streght of character and focused mind to take on the challenges of a sport that demands precision and superior athleticism.

programme.title: The Aviators S1 - "Chartright"

programme.title: The Aviators S1 - "Cessna"

programme.title: The Aviators S1 - "Sun 'n Fun Special"
programme.desc: We pay a visit to Spring Break for pilots in Lakeland, Florida.

programme.title: The Demolition Man S1 - "Newcastle"

programme.title: The Demolition Man S1 - "City of London"

programme.title: The Demolition Man S1 - "The Best of Part 2"
programme.desc: Brendan Moar looks back at the most interesting and dramatic moments that he’s encountered as The Demolition Man.

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S2 - "Anatomy of the House"

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S2 - "Extreme Buildings"
programme.desc: Throughout history, our ancestors have always strived to go higher, bigger, deeper, further - and this is reflected in the buildings and structures around our globe. But what secrets can these ancient structures reveal?

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S2 - "History's Hidden Marvels"
programme.desc: This episode explores some of history's most ingenious, yet lesser-known engineering solutions.

programme.title: Ancient Engineering S2 - "Ancient Waterways"
programme.desc: The ancient ancestors realized that building structures and machines to harness water to provide transport, power, drainage and irrigation was vital to the success of their civilizations.

programme.title: Survival Science S1 - "LOST!"
programme.desc: Nick and Laura head deep into the mountains to explore survival techniques that go far beyond anything they’ve learned before. Our courageous hosts subject themselves to intense survival training with the Survival Training School of California.

programme.title: Survival Science S1 - "ATV Accidents"
programme.desc: ATVs have allowed us to penetrate the wilderness like never before. But they’ve also made the backcountry a bit more dangerous. Laura and Nick rig up some dramatic, high-speed tests to see how accidents happen and what you can do to protect yourself.

programme.title: The World of Bridges S1 - "China"
programme.desc: We visit China's most famous Wind and Rain Bridge and the Ponte dei Salti in the Verzasca Valley that literally dates back to the Roman era.

programme.title: The World of Bridges S1 - "Wales"
programme.desc: The Millau Viaduct in the south of France is one of the highest bridge structures in the world while the Pontcysyllte Aqueduct, which stands high over the River Dee in northeast Wales, was built in the 19th century.

programme.title: The World of Bridges S1 - "India"
programme.desc: One of the most impressive steel bridges in the world can be found in Calcutta: the Howrah Bridge. Its predecessor is the Forth Bridge across the Firth of Forth, near the Scottish capital of Edinburgh.

programme.title: Quolls: Fast & Furious
programme.desc: Explore the life and habits of the elusive northern subspecies of the spotted-tailed quoll. Come with us on a journey into the personal life of this beautiful long-lost cousin of the Tasmanian tiger.

programme.title: Wild Iberia S1 - "Spring"
programme.desc: The sun heats the earth and life begins again. The animals wake from hibernation and busy themselves, building their nests in treetops and caves as they prepare to breed. All the spring babies are fighting for survival though their first days.

programme.title: Wild Iberia S1 - "Summer"
programme.desc: These are the days of thirst: it is hot. Only the mountains are cool; everywhere else suffers in heat between 40 and 50C. The rain is long forgotten. Each day is a search for shade and water.

programme.title: Wild Iberia S1 - "Autumn"
programme.desc: As the woods prepare to sleep, and mushrooms grow as the first rains fall, flocks of cranes migrate home to Spain from their summer season in the north. The stags clash their antlers in pursuit of the does; there is little time before winter sets in.

programme.title: Wild Iberia S1 - "Winter"
programme.desc: The unknown face of Spain. Snow, rain, clouds and cold envelop the land. The ibex migrate to the valleys, and wolves patrol the mountains as vultures circle the skies overhead.

programme.title: Wildlife Heroes S1 - "Maria Diekmann"
programme.desc: The Californian Maria Diekmann founded the Rare and Endangered Species Trust, REST in short, to provide care for injured and endangered animals.

programme.title: Wildlife Heroes S1 - "Stan Hutching"
programme.desc: For nearly 40 years, Stan Hutchings has been monitoring the migrations in The Great Bear Rainforest on Canada's northern West Coast, on behalf of the government.

programme.title: Animal Armoury S1 - "Teeth & Claws"
programme.desc: Bears, owls, and tigers use sharp claws for hunting, while baboons, wolves and woodchucks use their teeth.
